title: Operating Point Finder
description: Three challenges in which the learner predicts where illustrative fan Curve A crosses a duct system curve, followed by free exploration of the system resistance with a live operating point, BHP and stall-region flag.

educational.audience: Adult professional development: new application engineers, sales staff, representatives and facilities staff
educational.topic: Fan curve, system curve and the operating point
learningObjectives: The learner will solve for the operating point of an illustrative fan in a stated duct system by predicting where the fan curve and system curve intersect, to within ±300 CFM and ±0.15 in. wg.

accessibility.notes: describe() text (fallback mode); verdicts with the operating-point readouts, each new challenge and the summary announced through FP.announce (aria-live); ✓/✗ glyphs and solid/dashed borders pair with colour; fan and system curves differ by dash as well as colour; the stall region is hatched and labelled; predictions can be typed (Tab, Enter) as well as clicked on the chart.

controls.label: Check

simulation.modelType: numeric model (piecewise-linear fan curve intersected with a square-law system curve)
equations: Operating point: the airflow in 1 CFM steps from 0 to 16,000 CFM where |fan pressure - system pressure| is smallest
rules: Fan pressure and BHP between table points are linearly interpolated
Readouts: airflow to the nearest 10 CFM, pressure to two decimals, BHP to one decimal
An operating point below 4,000 CFM is flagged 'In the stall region: select a different fan.'
A prediction is correct when |predicted CFM - model CFM| <= 300 and |predicted pressure - model pressure| <= 0.15; two attempts per challenge
assumptions: Curve A is illustrative (Chapter 10), standard air, one fixed speed
The system curve has no fixed-pressure component and passes through zero
limitations: One fan at one speed; speed changes are covered by the Fan Law Calculator (Chapter 25)

sources: Curve A: illustrative fan curve table in Chapter 10, 'The Fan Curve' (not a Twin City Fan published rating)
Challenge systems and model intersections: Chapter 10, 'The Operating Point'
Square law for system resistance: standard fan engineering

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Commit a predicted intersection before it is drawn, then explore how the system curve moves the operating point
keyQuestions: Why does a loaded filter move the operating point left rather than right?
At what system resistance does this fan start to operate in its stall region?
commonMisconceptions: A fan always delivers its rated airflow, whatever the system
A dirtier, more resistant system makes the fan move more air
The system curve is a straight line
assessmentOpportunities: Running score shown as 'Challenges correct: n of 3'; mastery is 3 of 3 predictions within ±300 CFM and ±0.15 in. wg on the first attempt.
